newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Lodz city picks S&P for credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Lodz city picks S&P for credit rating.

text.p: The Polish city of Lodz picked the Standard & Poor's rating agency to give it a credit rating ahead of the city's potential eurobond issue, the city's spokesman said on Monday.
"In the just concluded tender Standar & Poor's was picked as the company which will give Lodz a credit rating," Witold Rosset told Reuters.
He said neither the time nor the size or currency of the possible eurobond have been chosen yet and Lodz would open a tender for the manager of the issue after it gets the rating.
"Certainly not before the summer vacations," Rosset said.
Earlier the city said it was mulling an issue of the bonds at the turn of the year and worth about 70 million zlotys.
If the Lodz issue materialises, it will be the first eurobond issued by a Polish city.
Poland has a credit rating of Baa3 from Moody's, BBB minus from Standard and Poor's and BBB from IBCA.
